title: Upu
summary: Upu (Apu/Aba/Apa/Apina/Ubi/Upi), was the region centered on the city of Damascus in the Late Bronze Age.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Upu (Apu/Aba/Apa/Apina/Ubi/Upi), was the region centered on the city of Damascus in the Late Bronze Age.

sections.title: History
sections.text: Damascus was named Dimašqu / Dimasqu / etc. (for example, "Dimaški"-(see: Niya Kingdom), in the letter correspondence.

sections.title: Battle of Megiddo
sections.text: Trevor Bryce (2012) states that Upu was among the cities/kingdoms fighting at the Battle of Megiddo against Thutmose III of Egypt (c. 1479 BC).

sections.title: Amarna period
sections.text:
In the Amarna Letters (c. 1350 BC), the region is mentioned in three letters, EA 53, 189, and 197 (EA is for 'el Amarna'). Etakkama of Qidšu (Kadesh) in the Beqaa (named the Amqu) is in partial control, between allegiance to Pharaoh, and conjoining forces with the king of Hatti.

The intrigue of the three Amarna letters appears to involve areas to the north and northwest of Damascus, into Lebanon and the Beqaa (named Amqu).

sections.title: EA 197. Mušihuna [client letter]
sections.text: The translation "[the land of Apu and] Damascus." is inaccurate and can cause confusion. It can be misunderstood as Apu and Damascus being two entities in a combined land. The transliteration kura-pi₂ and urudi-maš-qa, translates as Land of Api and city of Dimašqa, a more precise reading showing that the man went to the Land of Api and stayed in the city of Damascus.
